items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Early in 1927 I received an offer to join Lloyd Scott orchestra which I accepted... Frank had been asked to join Scott also and we both joined the band in Lexington, Ky. and played a dance without any rehearsal.

ctx.x: Early in 1927 I received an offer to join Lloyd Scott orchestra which I accepted because I had admired the band the first time I heard it and I also thought that I could read music better than I could when Alex asked to come and see him. I had refused another offer to join Speed Webb's orchestra who had been campaigning up state in New York and was getting ready to go to California.

When I told Helvey that I was going to join the Lloyd Scott orchestra he didn't want me to leave and threatened to make trouble for me even if he had to come to New York to do it. I had no idea if or when Scott would be going to New York, but I wanted to join the orchestra and told Helvey that I was leaving regardless of what he intended doing.

There was a tall trumpet player who had come to town from Virginia named Frank Newton and he had been playing with Clarence Paige for quite some time. Frank had been asked to join Scott also and we both joined the band in Lexington, Ky. and played a dance without any rehearsal. When Steve Dunn, the trumpet player that I had worked with in the Broadus band, saw me with Scott, he was so happy for me, that he hugged me like a long lost brother.
